## e1d032e35937

**Findings-only audit: reproduced shortcut and override-contract defects.** The
generator and reference rule remain unchanged at generator version `1.2.1`.
All counts below refer to generator SHA-256
`23c68d85e9025701d23088772d128f61c9833a443070e3b81ec021fe3f940ae3`.
Canonical program SHA-256 is
`02798fc4fa86c1dd6a331590595335059ab7d8cc599d9db1d69b05d9a19f7170`;
the supported Racket command confirms executed/catalog rule hash `02798fc4fa86`
and records executed rule-text SHA-256
`f509ebb71875b2b0e2da5fb7e300a5c203403cac1bd2b5ab6dc8682e1000a412`.

### A-e1d-1: Reproduced canvas-center shortcut; off-center coverage gap

The intentional diagnostic rival `fixed_horizontal_completion` fills every zero
with the value at the reversed column of its row. It does not locate the bar,
inspect its color, or determine which side contains the source:

```python
[[cell or reflected for cell, reflected in zip(row, reversed(row))]
 for row in grid]
```

The rival fits **3/3 usable canonical pairs**, including the canonical test pair.
Racket also reproduces all three canonical labels, and the validator accepts all
three inputs. On **60/60 unique generated inputs**, the rival exactly matches
Racket; all 60 pass `self_check`. The generated census uses seeds **0–19
inclusive**, sample index **0**, no overrides, separately for **easy, medium and
hard** difficulty (20 inputs per band). These are individual inputs, not lesson
windows. [comparison.json](checks/audit/e1d032e35937/comparison.json) retains every
case's identity and result.

This is more than a sampled correlation: every helpful `generate` branch makes
the width odd, sets `b = w // 2`, places source cells only to its left, and leaves
the right side blank. Consequently the rival agrees with the reference throughout
that actual helpful generator support. No generated helpful lesson can provide
a witness against it. The generator declares neither `CANONICAL_SHORTCUTS` nor
`LESSON_COMPETITORS`; the audit records their absence instead of claiming to have
tested declared competitors.

The retained **hand-constructed** witness is a 7×11 grid with its full-height
8-bar at zero-based column 4 and source cells `(1,1)=2`, `(3,2)=3`, `(5,0)=4`.
It passes `self_check` with no errors, satisfies the declared structural
invariants and lies within the documented shape/source-count ranges. Racket
reflects those cells to columns 7, 6 and 8. The rival disagrees at **12 cells**,
including adding an incorrect reflected bar. The complete input, actual Racket
output and rival output are in
[counterexample.json](checks/audit/e1d032e35937/counterexample.json), linked to
Racket result index 0 in [racket.json](checks/audit/e1d032e35937/racket.json).

**Domain distinction:** this witness belongs to the validator-accepted structural
domain and the written mirror-line rule, but **cannot be generated by the
unchanged helpful implementation**, which fixes the divider at the canvas center.
Its seed and sample index are therefore explicitly `null`. The finding is a
reproduced shortcut and coverage gap, not evidence of a wrong label on an actual
generated sample. Whether to expand the documented distribution with off-center
bars is a maintainer decision; no repair is included in this audit.

### A-e1d-2: Reproduced ignored palette and helpful-texture controls

For medium seeds **0–29 inclusive**, sample index **0**, every declared helpful
value of `palette_kind` and `texture`, and every integer **1–6** for
`palette_size` and `n_distinct_colors`, produces exactly the same grid as the
corresponding no-override call. Public `GenCtx.overrides_used()` reports the tested
override unconsumed in every case.

| Control | Values tested | Unchanged input comparisons |
|---|---|---:|
| `palette_kind` | default, warm, cool, varied | 120/120 |
| Helpful `texture` | default, warm, cool, varied | 120/120 |
| `palette_size` | 1–6 | 180/180 |
| `n_distinct_colors` | 1–6 | 180/180 |

These **600 comparisons** share **30 unique baseline inputs**; they are not 600
independent inputs or Racket label checks. In particular, requesting one distinct
source color yields 3–6 source colors across those seeds. The implementation
hardcodes palette `[2,3,4,6,7,9]` and never reads these helpful controls.
[probe.json](checks/audit/e1d032e35937/probe.json) records every value's denominator,
observed color-count range and context-consumption count.

### A-e1d-3: Reproduced exact-size and advertised-boundary inconsistencies

At seed **0**, sample index **0**, medium `grid_w=10` produces width **11** and
medium `grid_w=12` produces width **13**; hard `grid_w=14` produces width **15**.
All three returned grids pass `self_check`, despite missing the requested exact
width. The generator increments every even width after consuming the override.

The same seed/index with `source_count=1` raises `ValueError` under each of
`None`, easy, medium and hard difficulty, even though `AXES` advertises `1..12`.
Likewise, advertised-valid `grid_h=5` raises `ValueError` under all four settings.
These are **11 explicit contract probes**: three returned grids with incorrect
width and eight retained exceptions, not failed Racket applications. Exact
arguments, grids and exception strings are retained in
[probe.json](checks/audit/e1d032e35937/probe.json).

### Evidence and checked scope

The audit read the generator, canonical task row, summary, working notes and
associated-notes file. The latter contains no entries. It checked all canonical
pairs, 60 generated inputs, one structural-domain hand witness, 600 control
comparisons and 11 explicit boundary/width probes. The supported reference call
executes **64 inputs with zero authority errors**. No full battery, exported
lesson census or new safety approval is claimed.

Exact replay commands, packet-relative working directories and observed exit
statuses are in [commands.json](checks/audit/e1d032e35937/commands.json); all three
recorded commands exited 0. Racket's payload runs from `repo`, as also recorded
in its report. The reusable probe is
[audit_probe.py](checks/audit/e1d032e35937/audit_probe.py). Source identities,
input identities and genuine stdout/stderr are retained in the adjacent evidence
files. No generator, rule or model-visible solve file was edited.

## e1d032e35937

**Findings-only: reproduced an unresolved canvas-center shortcut and three override-contract failures.** Generator v1.2.1 and its Racket authority were left unchanged. All observations below are fresh measurements of generator SHA-256 `23c68d85e9025701d23088772d128f61c9833a443070e3b81ec021fe3f940ae3`. The existing audit `review-bf9d7c5f13da3e98:v0001` supplied leads; its reported counts were not reused. The exact canonical record, current generator identity, tested arguments and local validator results are retained in [probe.json](checks/audit/e1d032e35937/probe.json).

The canonical program SHA-256 is `02798fc4fa86c1dd6a331590595335059ab7d8cc599d9db1d69b05d9a19f7170`. The supported public Racket command reports matching executed/catalog rule hash `02798fc4fa86` and executed rule-text SHA-256 `f509ebb71875b2b0e2da5fb7e300a5c203403cac1bd2b5ab6dc8682e1000a412`. It successfully labelled **22/22 inputs**, with no authority errors. [racket.json](checks/audit/e1d032e35937/racket.json)

### A-e1d-1 — Reproduced teaching coverage gap: the visible bar can be ignored

The intentional rival `fixed_canvas_reflection` fills every zero using the opposite canvas column. It neither locates the bar nor reads its color:

```python
[[value or reflected for value, reflected in zip(row, reversed(row))]
 for row in grid]
```

It matches Racket on **18/18 unique generated inputs**: the Cartesian product of difficulties **easy, medium, hard**, seeds **0, 1, 17**, and sample indices **0, 1**, with no overrides. It also matches **3/3 usable canonical pairs**, including the canonical test pair; Racket reproduces all three stored labels. All 21 inputs pass `self_check`. These are individual input checks, not lesson windows. [comparison.json](checks/audit/e1d032e35937/comparison.json)

Source inspection explains the systematic correlation: every helpful branch makes the width odd, places the bar at `w // 2`, selects source cells only to its left, and leaves the right blank. On this entire helpful support, reflection across the bar equals reflection across the canvas center. Consequently, increasing the number of examples from this unchanged support cannot refute this rival. The generator declares no `CANONICAL_SHORTCUTS` or `LESSON_COMPETITORS`; the retained probe records their absence and labels its rival as an intentional audit hypothesis. [audit_probe.py](checks/audit/e1d032e35937/audit_probe.py)

A fresh **hand-constructed 8×9 witness** places the full-height 8-bar at zero-based column **3**, with sources `(1,1)=2`, `(3,2)=3`, and `(5,0)=4`. `self_check` accepts it with `[]`. Racket adds `(1,5)=2`, `(3,4)=3`, and `(5,6)=4`. The rival reflects around canvas column 4 instead, including creating an incorrect second bar, and differs from Racket at **13 cells**. The complete input, actual Racket output, rival output and cell differences are retained in [counterexample.json](checks/audit/e1d032e35937/counterexample.json), linked to Racket result index 0.

**Domain distinction:** the witness satisfies the stated invariants and documented shape/source-count ranges; its dimensions and count also lie within the easy draw ranges. It is nevertheless outside the actual helpful generator support because the implementation fixes the divider at the center. Its seed and sample index are therefore `null`, not an invented generator recipe. This is a reproduced shortcut/coverage gap, not a wrong Racket label on a generated sample. Whether off-center examples should be added, or the intended domain explicitly narrowed to centered bars, remains a maintainer decision. No repair or safety approval is included.

### A-e1d-2 — Reproduced ignored palette controls

At **seed 17, sample index 0, medium**, the no-override input has **five distinct source colors**. Every declared helpful value below returns exactly that same input, passes `self_check`, and is absent from the public `GenCtx.overrides_used()` result:

| Control | Exact values tested | Unchanged and unconsumed |
|---|---|---:|
| `palette_kind` | default, warm, cool, varied | 4/4 |
| Helpful `texture` | default, warm, cool, varied | 4/4 |
| `palette_size` | 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 | 6/6 |
| `n_distinct_colors` | 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 | 6/6 |

The **20 comparisons share one baseline input**; they are not 20 independent grids or additional Racket applications. In particular, both one-color controls return five colors. The code hardcodes palette `[2,3,4,6,7,9]` and never consumes these helpful controls. Exact inputs, arguments and context observations are in [probe.json](checks/audit/e1d032e35937/probe.json).

### A-e1d-3 — Reproduced width and advertised-boundary mismatches

At **seed 0, sample index 0**, medium `grid_w=10` returns width **11**, and hard `grid_w=14` returns width **15**. Both returned inputs pass `self_check`. These values are consumed as width overrides and then incremented by the implementation, so the returned dimensions differ from the requested exact dimensions. [probe.json](checks/audit/e1d032e35937/probe.json)

At that same seed/index, each of `source_count=1`, `source_count=12`, and `grid_h=5` raises `ValueError` under every tested difficulty setting: **None, easy, medium, hard**. These are **12/12 retained exceptions**. `AXES` advertises `source_count` as `1..12` and `grid_h` as `5..15`, yet those boundary values are outside every branch's draw bounds. The one-source declaration also conflicts with `self_check` requiring at least two sources. The exact exception strings are retained; no failed generation was counted as an input or Racket application. [probe.json](checks/audit/e1d032e35937/probe.json)

### Tested scope and replay

This audit read the current generator, summary, notes, review index, empty associated-notes file, and exact canonical task record. It checked all three canonical pairs, 18 generated inputs, one structural-domain hand witness, 20 control comparisons, 12 exception probes and two returned-width probes. **22/22 distinct inputs passed the local validator and Racket execution.** The measured defects remain failures despite the replay commands exiting 0: those exits mean the reported audit observations were reproduced.

The three executed commands, `cwd: packet_root`, absolute invocation directory, effective payload directory (`WORK/repo`), exit codes and stdout/stderr paths are in [command_receipts.json](checks/audit/e1d032e35937/command_receipts.json). The executable [run_audit.py](checks/audit/e1d032e35937/run_audit.py) runs prepare → public Racket apply → compare; [audit_probe.py](checks/audit/e1d032e35937/audit_probe.py) implements the observations. Replay from the outer packet root into a fresh evidence directory:

```bash
python3 WORK/checks/audit/e1d032e35937/run_audit.py \
  --packet-root . \
  --out-dir WORK/checks/audit/e1d032e35937/replay
```

No full battery, isolated audit preset, production lesson assembly, query-rotation check or natural solve failure is claimed. No generator, shared tool, catalog, assignment or solve-lane file was edited.
